viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
We’ve been busy shipping 🚢 Here’s a recap of the last couple of weeks:

— Gemini 4 Neon, our newest model that brings frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows

— Gemini 4 Hydrogen, our model for speed and efficiency in everyday coding and agentic workflows

— Gemini 4 Carbon, our model for your hardest long-horizon projects and deep research

— Genie 4, @GoogleDeepMind’s most realistic interactive world model featuring real-time scene editing and adaptive native audio, now available in Project Genie (with a new creation agent and gallery) and for the first time in the Gemini API and @GoogleAIStudio

— Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, now with native voice editing that lets developers build experiences where users can edit, rephrase, and translate existing text in a single step using just their voice, via the Gemini API in @GoogleAIStudio

— Gemini Robotics 2.5, @GoogleDeepMind’s most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date

— AlphaGenome 2, @GoogleDeepMind’s new AI model that zooms in on specific cells to help scientists understand what drives disease

— Stitch Loop, a new @stitchbygoogle experiment from @GoogleLabs that monitors production data and runs continuous loops to improve your designed product until goals are met

top_three.author: Bloomberg
top_three.article_content:
AI (Artificial Intelligence) letters and robot hand are placed on computer motherboard in this illustration taken, June 23, 2023. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Nov 20 : Coding startup Cognition AI is in funding talks at a $75 billion valuation, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The company is considering raising $2 billion or more in the latest round, the report said, adding that the talks were ongoing and the details could change.

The news comes about two months after Cognition raised $2 billion in a Series E funding round at a valuation of $48 billion. The round was led by new investors Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, alongside existing backers Founders Fund, General Catalyst, and Avenir.

Cognition did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

The company is an AI startup that develops autonomous software-engineering agents, which can plan, write, test and deploy code with limited human intervention.

The company was valued at $26 billion in a funding round in May, when it raised $1 billion.

top_three.title: OpenAI makes it much harder for attackers to extract how its latest AI models think
top_three.title_en: OpenAI makes it much harder for attackers to extract how its latest AI models think
top_three.author: Matthias Bastian
top_three.article_content:
OpenAI has sharply tightened safeguards against extracting internal reasoning from GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. In internal automated tests, attacks pulling protected reasoning from prior requests dropped from a 54.0 percent success rate on GPT-6 Astra to 0.2 percent on GPT-6.2 Astra. Attacks on active requests fell from 22.9 to 0.9 percent, OpenAI says. The company is now bringing selected improvements to GPT-6 Astra, too.

The defenses work on two levels. For individual requests, the systems combine targeted training, input and output filters for messages and tool calls, and API blocks that stop older models from reading protected reasoning. Against coordinated campaigns, OpenAI bans thousands to tens of thousands of accounts weekly.

Attack success rate (ASR) in adaptive black-box red teaming against GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.2 Astra, aggregated across six attacker models. Lower is better.

Anthropic is fighting systematic distillation attacks as well, also banning tens of thousands of accounts to curb the theft of internal reasoning, reportedly succeeding in 90 to 99 percent of cases. Anthropic has also called for a coordinated response from industry and policymakers.

top_three.title_zh: OpenAI强化推理层防护，抑制大模型蒸馏攻击
top_three.summary_zh: OpenAI大幅提升GPT-6.2系列模型安全性，通过多层过滤机制将推理数据泄露攻击成功率降至0.2%以下

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI针对GPT-6.2 Astra与GPT-6.2 Sol模型部署了分层防护机制，通过针对性训练、输入输出过滤及API拦截策略，将针对推理数据的黑盒攻击成功率从54%大幅削减至0.2%。该举措旨在阻断通过合成数据蒸馏提取模型核心推理模式的攻击链路，并配合每周对数万违规账户的封禁实现全链条防御。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI has deployed layered security mechanisms for GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models, reducing the success rate of black-box inference-extraction attacks from 54% to under 0.2% through targeted training, input/output filtering, and API access restrictions. These measures are designed to neutralize distillation attacks that attempt to reconstruct core reasoning paths, supplemented by the weekly suspension of tens of thousands of illicit accounts.

elements_zh.who: OpenAI（模型开发者）
elements_zh.where: 企业内部模型安全生产环境
elements_zh.what: 部署针对推理数据的多层防护架构，包括输入/输出过滤、API访问拦截及针对性强化训练
elements_zh.why: 防止攻击者通过模型蒸馏技术窃取核心推理逻辑，保护模型技术壁垒

elements_en.what: Implemented layered defenses including I/O filtering, API blocking, and adversarial training
elements_en.why: To prevent distillation-based theft of internal reasoning logic and protect proprietary model intellectual property

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 大模型竞争已进入以‘知识产权保全’为核心的防蒸馏防御战阶段。随着模型推理逻辑的价值攀升，闭源大模型厂商正通过强化API黑盒化与流量合规清洗，从底层逻辑上切断廉价获取高质量蒸馏数据的路径，这将迫使后续开源模型生态面临更严苛的训练数据合规审查压力。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Competition in the large model sector has shifted toward intellectual property preservation via anti-distillation defense. As reasoning logic becomes a primary value driver, proprietary model vendors are increasingly 'black-boxing' APIs and cleansing traffic to block cost-effective distillation, likely forcing the open-source community to face significantly higher scrutiny regarding training data provenance.

top_three.title: Many Etsy Sellers Close Up Shop Over Site’s New A.I. Policy
top_three.title_en: Many Etsy Sellers Close Up Shop Over Site’s New A.I. Policy
top_three.author: Reggie Ugwu
top_three.article_content:
Many longtime owners of shops on Etsy, the online marketplace known for its handmade goods, said this week that they had left the site over a policy change that they said leaves them vulnerable to exploitation by artificial intelligence companies.

Language in Etsy’s new terms, set to take effect on Dec. 16, says the company and its “third party partners and vendors” reserve the right to use sellers’ content to “develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.”

The terms say that Etsy and its partners will use such technologies in part to improve the platform and keep it safe for users. The previous version of the terms did not include a clause about using content for artificial intelligence.

“Etsy decided that selling on their platform now means letting them train AI on our artwork AND resell that data to third parties, with no way to opt out,” Aaron Millard, an illustrator, wrote in an Instagram post announcing that he was deleting the shop that he has run for nearly a decade. “My work took years to learn and create. I won’t let it be stolen.”

Kristen and Geoff Zephyrus, the founders of the home goods and stationary brand Cognitive Surplus, which has sold its products on Etsy for 13 years, also deleted their shop. In an Instagram post, they accused the company of claiming “perpetual, free, boundless permission to not only train AI on our art, but also to resell the data for profit.”

“For Etsy to be helping to train algorithms with our human content is just unimaginably awful,” Kristen Zephyrus said in an interview. “We don’t want anything to do with that.”

In a statement posted to Etsy’s website on Monday, James Ossman, the company’s vice president for customer operations, addressed the site’s sellers directly.

Etsy will not “use your content to train A.I. models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity,” Ossman wrote. He cited the development of fraud detection tools and advertisements on the site as among the reasons for granting third parties access to sellers’ content.

A representative for Etsy did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday.

Many publicly traded internet companies like Etsy have been caught between pressure from shareholders to embrace artificial intelligence and the ire of users who reject the technology.

Big bets by major firms and their investors on the A.I. revolution have helped the U.S. stock market set records in recent years. But Americans in general are much less enthusiastic. A Gallup poll from the summer found that nearly 40 percent of Americans feel that A.I. does more harm than good. Big bets by major firms and their investors on the A.I. revolution have helped the U.S. stock market set records in recent years. But Americans in general are much less enthusiastic. A Gallup poll from the summer found that nearly 40 percent of Americans feel that A.I. does more harm than good. Many of the Democratic political candidates who swept into power during the midterm elections this month campaigned explicitly against A.I. companies and data centers.

Etsy, which was founded in 2005 to help independent artisans find customers online, is no stranger to user revolt. In 2022, more than 20,000 Etsy sellers went on strike to protest a 30 percent increase in its base-line sales fee, to 6.5 percent from 5 percent. In October, the company announced tighter restrictions on so-called A.I. slop after many users decried such content.

elements_zh.where: Etsy平台服务条款更新
elements_zh.what: 强制授权平台及第三方利用卖家作品训练AI模型，且未提供拒绝选项
elements_zh.why: 平台面临股东压力需拥抱AI技术，而创作者面临知识产权变现与流失风险

elements_en.who: Etsy, James Ossman (VP of Customer Operations)
elements_en.what: Compulsory authorization for AI training using seller data without opt-out options
elements_en.why: Institutional pressure to integrate AI vs. creator rights protection

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此事件反映了内容平台在AI转型期的合规性危机，即平台“数据所有权”与创作者“知识产权”的结构性矛盾。若缺乏透明的授权机制与收益对价，平台通过AI榨取长尾内容价值将导致生态失衡，最终造成高质量创作资源的流失与社区价值的毁灭性衰减。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident highlights the structural conflict between platform data-mining mandates and creator IP rights during the AI transition. Without transparent authorization and value-sharing mechanisms, the forced extraction of creator data to train AI risks long-term ecological depletion and the exodus of the platform's core creative capital.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 电商平台Etsy宣布将于12月16日生效的新条款，规定公司及其第三方合作伙伴有权使用平台创作者内容进行AI模型训练与测试。此举引发艺术家与独立品牌主大规模抗议，尽管Etsy副总裁James Ossman回应称相关数据仅用于欺诈检测与广告优化，但因缺乏退出机制及对知识产权流失的担忧，导致大量资深卖家注销店铺。

This prompted widespread backlash and shop closures from creators, despite claims from James Ossman, VP of customer operations, that data use is restricted to fraud detection and advertising, as users remain concerned about the lack of opt-out mechanisms and potential IP exploitation.

topic_focus.title_zh: Anthropic数学家Levent Alpöge声称利用Claude破解黎曼猜想
topic_focus.title_en: Anthropic's Levent Alpöge Claims Claude Solved the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis
topic_focus.summary_zh: Anthropic数学家莱文特·阿尔波格 (Levent Alpöge) 公开宣布在Claude辅助下证明了数学史上最著名的黎曼猜想，并以Lean编程语言发布了证明过程。此举若获证实，将标志着AI从工具演进为解决顶级科学难题的核心智力引擎。
topic_focus.summary_en: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced he used Claude to prove the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis, publishing the result in the Lean language. If verified, this marks a pivot from AI as a productivity tool to a core engine for solving historic scientific enigmas.

perspective_pro.role_zh: 🟢 演进派 / AI科研赋能支持者
perspective_pro.point_zh: AI能够处理人类数学家难以跨越的计算复杂度与形式化验证，黎曼猜想的证明若属实，将是AI辅助发现的里程碑。
perspective_pro.point_en: AI overcomes the computational complexity that limits human mathematicians; this proof would be a milestone in machine-aided scientific discovery.

perspective_con.role_zh: 🔴 工业理性派 / 数学严谨性怀疑者
perspective_con.point_zh: 目前证明仍处于早期验证阶段，AI模型产生的逻辑链可能存在‘幻觉式逻辑陷阱’，必须通过顶级数学同行评审的严格校验。
perspective_con.point_en: The proof is in the early verification stage; AI models often generate 'hallucinatory logic traps' that require rigorous peer review by the math community.

linked_tweets.author: Chubby♨️
linked_tweets.content_zh:
今天创造了历史。人类将在回顾 2026 年时思考：这是我们跨过的门槛，从那一刻起，每个人的未来都将永远改变。

人们可能在 2025 年底通过 Claude Code 第一次感觉到事情正在发生变化，当时代理人工智能对他们来说变得真正有形。 2026 年上半年，事情加速发展。模型发布越来越频繁，大家都能感受到模型之间的差距和改进越来越明显。然而到了2026年下半年，却出现了质的飞跃。这不再只是模型变得更好了。人工智能产生的见解、结果、产出和科学解决方案变得更加令人印象深刻，今天它们可能已经达到了绝对的顶峰。

OpenAI 率先解决了纳维-斯托克斯问题，这是人类在很长一段时间内未能解决的千年奖问题。几周后，他们发表了 300 多个开放数学问题的结果，其中许多问题几十年来都没有得到解决。整个科学界都惊呆了，震惊不已。但今天 Anthropic 更进一步。 Levent Alpöge 与 Claude 合作，几乎肯定证明了黎曼猜想。这实在是难以用言语来形容，令人难以置信，深不可测。我想说，今天是超级智能的证明。 167 年来一直没有解决的最伟大的数学问题之一，数学和科学的圣杯，即使不是最伟大的，也已经陨落了。接下来，每个人都应该清楚，所有其他问题也会随之下降。

我们知道，人工智能模型的发展不断向前发展，而这只是迈向更好模型的第一步。如果黎曼假设今天已经得到证明，那么根本不知道更好的模型会解决什么问题。达里奥·阿莫迪表示，人工智能很可能会治愈疾病，甚至可能治愈所有疾病。尽管这是两个不同的科学学科，但这些突破的意义表明，这种情况变得越来越有可能。 2026 年将作为一个转折点载入人类历史，奇点变得有形的那一刻。 2027 年将是奇点以全力和全面影响力进入现实的一年。

我感到震惊和兴奋，不知道该怎么想。但内心深处却感到喜悦。

这一天对我们所有人来说都是最美好的日子之一。
linked_tweets.content_en:
History was made today. Humanity will look back on 2026 and think: this was the threshold we crossed, the moment the future changed for everyone, forever.

People probably first sensed that something was shifting in late 2025 with Claude Code, when agentic AI became truly tangible for them. In the first half of 2026, things picked up speed. Model releases became more frequent, and everyone could feel the gaps between models and the improvements becoming more and more tangible. In the second half of 2026, however, there was a qualitative leap. It was no longer just the models getting better. It was the insights, the results, the outputs, the scientific solutions produced with AI that became more impressive, and today they have probably reached their absolute peak.

OpenAI led the way and solved the Navier-Stokes problem, a Millennium Prize Problem that humans had failed to solve for a very, very long time. A few weeks later, they published results on more than 300 open mathematical problems, many of which had also gone unsolved for decades. The entire scientific world was stunned, frozen in shock. But today Anthropic went a step further. Levent Alpöge, working with Claude, has almost certainly proven the Riemann Hypothesis. This is, and it’s hard to put into words, incredible and unfathomable. Today, I would say, is the proof of superintelligence. One of the greatest mathematical problems, if not the greatest, unsolved for 167 years, the holy grail of mathematics and science, has fallen. And it follows, and this should be clear to everyone, that all other problems will fall too.

We know that the development of AI models keeps moving forward relentlessly, and that this is just one step on the path to ever better models. And if the Riemann Hypothesis has already been proven today, there is simply no telling what even better models will solve. Dario Amodei said that AI will in all likelihood cure diseases, perhaps even all diseases. And although these are two different scientific disciplines, the significance of these breakthroughs shows that this is becoming more and more likely. 2026 will go down in human history as a turning point, the moment the singularity became tangible. And 2027 will be the year the singularity breaks into reality with full force and full impact.

I am in shock and excitement and I don't know what to think. But deep inside if feel joy. 

This day is one of the best days ever for all of us.

news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
AI (Artificial Intelligence) letters and robot hand are placed on computer motherboard in this illustration taken, June 23, 2023. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Nov 20 : Coding startup Cognition AI is in funding talks at a $75 billion valuation, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The company is considering raising $2 billion or more in the latest round, the report said, adding that the talks were ongoing and the details could change.

The news comes about two months after Cognition raised $2 billion in a Series E funding round at a valuation of $48 billion. The round was led by new investors Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, alongside existing backers Founders Fund, General Catalyst, and Avenir.

Cognition did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

The company is an AI startup that develops autonomous software-engineering agents, which can plan, write, test and deploy code with limited human intervention.

The company was valued at $26 billion in a funding round in May, when it raised $1 billion.

news.title: Many Etsy Sellers Close Up Shop Over Site’s New A.I. Policy
news.title_en: Many Etsy Sellers Close Up Shop Over Site’s New A.I. Policy
news.author: Reggie Ugwu
news.article_content:
Many longtime owners of shops on Etsy, the online marketplace known for its handmade goods, said this week that they had left the site over a policy change that they said leaves them vulnerable to exploitation by artificial intelligence companies.

Language in Etsy’s new terms, set to take effect on Dec. 16, says the company and its “third party partners and vendors” reserve the right to use sellers’ content to “develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.”

The terms say that Etsy and its partners will use such technologies in part to improve the platform and keep it safe for users. The previous version of the terms did not include a clause about using content for artificial intelligence.

“Etsy decided that selling on their platform now means letting them train AI on our artwork AND resell that data to third parties, with no way to opt out,” Aaron Millard, an illustrator, wrote in an Instagram post announcing that he was deleting the shop that he has run for nearly a decade. “My work took years to learn and create. I won’t let it be stolen.”

Kristen and Geoff Zephyrus, the founders of the home goods and stationary brand Cognitive Surplus, which has sold its products on Etsy for 13 years, also deleted their shop. In an Instagram post, they accused the company of claiming “perpetual, free, boundless permission to not only train AI on our art, but also to resell the data for profit.”

“For Etsy to be helping to train algorithms with our human content is just unimaginably awful,” Kristen Zephyrus said in an interview. “We don’t want anything to do with that.”

In a statement posted to Etsy’s website on Monday, James Ossman, the company’s vice president for customer operations, addressed the site’s sellers directly.

Etsy will not “use your content to train A.I. models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity,” Ossman wrote. He cited the development of fraud detection tools and advertisements on the site as among the reasons for granting third parties access to sellers’ content.

A representative for Etsy did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday.

Many publicly traded internet companies like Etsy have been caught between pressure from shareholders to embrace artificial intelligence and the ire of users who reject the technology.

Big bets by major firms and their investors on the A.I. revolution have helped the U.S. stock market set records in recent years. But Americans in general are much less enthusiastic. A Gallup poll from the summer found that nearly 40 percent of Americans feel that A.I. does more harm than good. “For Etsy to be helping to train algorithms with our human content is just unimaginably awful,” Kristen Zephyrus said in an interview. “We don’t want anything to do with that.”

Many publicly traded internet companies like Etsy have been caught between pressure from shareholders to embrace artificial intelligence and the ire of users who reject the technology.

Big bets by major firms and their investors on the A.I. revolution have helped the U.S. stock market set records in recent years. But Americans in general are much less enthusiastic. A Gallup poll from the summer found that nearly 40 percent of Americans feel that A.I. does more harm than good. Many of the Democratic political candidates who swept into power during the midterm elections this month campaigned explicitly against A.I. companies and data centers.

Etsy, which was founded in 2005 to help independent artisans find customers online, is no stranger to user revolt. In 2022, more than 20,000 Etsy sellers went on strike to protest a 30 percent increase in its base-line sales fee, to 6.5 percent from 5 percent. In October, the company announced tighter restrictions on so-called A.I. slop after many users decried such content.
news.title_zh: Etsy新规引发创作者集体出走
news.summary_zh: Etsy因调整服务条款，授权第三方调用卖家数据训练AI，导致资深商家关闭店铺抵制

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 电商平台Etsy宣布将于12月16日生效的新条款，规定公司及其第三方合作伙伴有权使用平台创作者内容进行AI模型训练与测试。此举引发艺术家与独立品牌主大规模抗议，尽管Etsy副总裁James Ossman回应称相关数据仅用于欺诈检测与广告优化，但因缺乏退出机制及对知识产权流失的担忧，导致大量资深卖家注销店铺。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Etsy has introduced new terms of service, effective December 16, allowing the company and its third-party partners to use seller content for training and testing AI models. This prompted widespread backlash and shop closures from creators, despite claims from James Ossman, VP of customer operations, that data use is restricted to fraud detection and advertising, as users remain concerned about the lack of opt-out mechanisms and potential IP exploitation.

elements_zh.who: Etsy（电商平台），James Ossman（客户运营副总裁）
elements_zh.where: Etsy平台服务条款更新
elements_zh.what: 强制授权平台及第三方利用卖家作品训练AI模型，且未提供拒绝选项
elements_zh.why: 平台面临股东压力需拥抱AI技术，而创作者面临知识产权变现与流失风险

elements_en.who: Etsy, James Ossman (VP of Customer Operations)
elements_en.what: Compulsory authorization for AI training using seller data without opt-out options
elements_en.why: Institutional pressure to integrate AI vs. creator rights protection

ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident highlights the structural conflict between platform data-mining mandates and creator IP rights during the AI transition. Without transparent authorization and value-sharing mechanisms, the forced extraction of creator data to train AI risks long-term ecological depletion and the exodus of the platform's core creative capital.

This prompted widespread backlash and shop closures from creators, despite claims from James Ossman, VP of customer operations, that data use is restricted to fraud detection and advertising, as users remain concerned about the lack of opt-out mechanisms and potential IP exploitation.

ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 此事件反映了内容平台在AI转型期的合规性危机，即平台“数据所有权”与创作者“知识产权”的结构性矛盾。若缺乏透明的授权机制与收益对价，平台通过AI榨取长尾内容价值将导致生态失衡，最终造成高质量创作资源的流失与社区价值的毁灭性衰减。

news.title: Canada Retail Sales Tracking Largest Decline Since Feb. 2025
news.title_en: Canada Retail Sales Tracking Largest Decline Since Feb. 2025
news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
Canadian retail spending is expected to have declined in October, following a 0.8% increase in September led by gasoline stations and fuel vendors.

A preliminary estimate points to a 1.5% decrease in retail sales last month, which would be the largest decline since February 2025.

Sales in September increased in five out of nine subsectors, and rose by 6.9% at gasoline stations and fuel vendors. That increase was largely driven by higher prices, as sales in volume terms increased by a more modest 1.6%.

Economists surveyed by Bloomberg had expected retail sales increased by 0.7% in September.

Core retail sales, which exclude gasoline stations and fuel vendors as well as motor vehicle and parts dealers, increased by 0.1%. In volume terms, sales were also up by 0.1%.

The largest decline in core retail sales was food and beverage retailers, which was led by a 0.5% decline at grocery stores, following a 1% increase in August.

Building material and garden equipment and supplies dealers declined by 1.3%, while furniture, home furnishings electronics and appliances retailers decreased by the same magnitude.

Meanwhile, retail sales increased by 1.2% in the third quarter. In volume terms, they rose by 1% over the three-month period.

The expected decline in October retail sales provides further evidence of weakening to start the fourth quarter, said CIBC senior economist Andrew Grantham.

“While the 1.5% decline estimated for October will partly reflect lower gasoline prices, most of that move lower in pump prices has actually occurred in November rather than October, and as a result this advance estimate suggests a decline in volumes as well,” Grantham said in a note to investors.

The Canadian economy — including consumer spending — has remained largely resilient throughout the U.S. trade war. However, growth is expected to slow in the second half of the year after the dispute escalated and more tariffs were imposed by both countries.

The labour market has also shown signs of weakness, as employment has failed to grow this year. Servus Credit Union chief economist Charles St-Arnaud said the stagnant labour market in recent months may be to blame for weaker retail sales.

“This is another indicator that suggests that the Canadian economy is losing momentum going into the last few months of 2026. The weakness suggests the Bank of Canada should take a pause to better assess the situation before hike again, especially with some fuel prices easing in recent weeks,” St-Arnaud said in an email.

Despite the expected slowdown, the Bank of Canada raised interest rates in October to clamp down on inflationary pressures from higher energy prices. Traders in overnight swaps put the odds of a hike in December at about 60%, which would further weigh on spending.

–...

Despite resilient growth in the third quarter, the combination of escalated trade disputes and a stagnant labor market has dampened fourth-quarter momentum, prompting analysts to expect a pause in rate hikes by the Bank of Canada.

news.title: TML releases Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights 26.4B-parameter transformer that loops middle layers three times per token for better reasoning with fewer tokens (Thinking Machines Lab)
news.title_en: TML releases Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights 26.4B-parameter transformer that loops middle layers three times per token for better reasoning with fewer tokens (Thinking Machines Lab)
news.author: Thinking Machines Lab
news.article_content:
Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.

Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It runs faster than similarly performing models as well.

Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping. Looping allows the model to reason longer without writing its reasoning down, which matters for monitoring: our ability to oversee and understand what the model does by reading its chain of thought (CoT).

We measured the impact of looping on both performance and monitorability with Inkling 2 Mini and a research-specific variable-loop variant we are releasing alongside it. The variable-loop model’s no-CoT time horizon improved from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds with three, and its performance on a benchmark of serial reasoning kept improving out to ten loops—twice as many as it was trained with. The model’s chain of thought grew shorter with more loops but stayed legible throughout. The model didn’t trend higher on tests of agentic sabotage as loops were added.

We’re excited to offer some of the first models with looped architecture available to researchers. The variable-loop model was used for our monitorability experiments as it allows for cleaner comparisons between different looping depths.

Most of Inkling 2 Mini’s weights were trained and are deployed natively in NVFP4, with the last four layers in MXFP8. The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers. Our researchers took Inkling 2 Mini on a flight, where it ran offline on a MacBook Pro and built a playable flight simulator in a few minutes.

Open video: PlaneBench flight simulator demo, screen with phone video inset0:0015× Loading the flight simulator Inkling 2 Mini built… To try the flight simulator, open this page on desktop. Inkling 2 Mini is released with open weights and is available on Tinker today for inference and customization.

Inkling 2 Mini’s strengths mirror those of Inkling 2 Small: it does best on long-horizon agentic work and is the best among open-weights models of similar size on most tasks we measured.

news.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
news.title_en: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
news.author: Dan Goodin
news.article_content:
Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

### Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations

To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of AWS access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible.

The findings are striking. They included:

Evidence that at least three AI providers were compromised by attackers who used their access to siphon prompts they received

Multiple resellers in the inference marketplace that logged the prompts and somehow passed them along to people who used the credentials

Multiple cases of AI providers not following end-user privacy settings embedded into flags specifying terms such as Zero Data Retention (ZDR) or “no data collection”

“We sent nearly two million AI prompts containing unique, trackable secrets to AI providers, then watched where those secrets surfaced,” Moore, the chief research officer of security firm Dragos, wrote Thursday. “What we found revealed security breaches, prompt theft, and widespread failures to protect customer data.”

Although prompts are encrypted in transit, they are decrypted at each hop inside the large inference reseller network. news.summary_en: HD Moore, Chief Research Officer at Dragos, uncovered major security flaws in the AI supply chain by injecting 2 million trackable 'canary' secrets into AI prompts sent via routing services. The investigation found evidence of prompt theft, disregard for zero-data-retention (ZDR) settings, and unauthorized logging of user prompts by intermediaries, posing significant compliance risks.
paragraphs: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.
### Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations

To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of AWS access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible.
The findings are striking. They included:
Evidence that at least three AI providers were compromised by attackers who used their access to siphon prompts they received
Multiple resellers in the inference marketplace that logged the prompts and somehow passed them along to people who used the credentials
Multiple cases of AI providers not following end-user privacy settings embedded into flags specifying terms such as Zero Data Retention (ZDR) or “no data collection”

“We sent nearly two million AI prompts containing unique, trackable secrets to AI providers, then watched where those secrets surfaced,” Moore, the chief research officer of security firm Dragos, wrote Thursday. “What we found revealed security breaches, prompt theft, and widespread failures to protect customer data.”

Although prompts are encrypted in transit, they are decrypted at each hop inside the large inference reseller network. The prompt is first sent to an AI router, which reads the plaintext in it to determine the most suitable inference providers to handle the request. Often, the prompt is then sent to a pool of available models, which sometimes run inside different hosting providers. Prompts can also pass from one AI router (such as Vercel) to another one (e.g. OpenRouter). Each one of these players is likely to log the prompt and store it for as long as its policies call for (if not indefinitely).
### The Wild West in the age of AI
The most concerning of the findings was the breach of three separate hosting providers. The attackers who compromised one of the providers reused “a couple hundred” of the AWS keys. Moore wrote:

Each key was sent in exactly one request to one provider, all within a few short windows in late October, and every request we sent during those windows was stolen. Some of the stolen keys came from requests that the provider rejected before a model ever ran—this tells us that the attacker was copying requests at the provider’s front door, and not somewhere deeper in the inference stack. In the other two breaches, some of the stolen requests were marked as ZDR. A privacy flag doesn’t help when the attacker is already inside.

Parties tied to the hack of these three providers then tested each key, in some cases within hours of being seeded, to see what kind of resources it gave access to. The parties looked through S3 buckets, secrets managers, and parameter stores in search of still more credentials. They also tried to enable hosted models in AWS Bedrock and added their own IAM users to maintain access. In all, the stolen bait keys were used “tens of thousands” of times in AWS API calls.

Secrets sent to two of the hacked providers were quickly used together, almost immediately, from the same rented server. That means the providers were almost certainly compromised by the same adversary.

As noted earlier, some of the secrets were stolen by the resellers themselves. To lure prompts to their servers, they offered low prices. Then they turned on request logging, and waited. Moore identified them by sending requests to the same model through different sellers. When credentials were later reused when sent through one seller and not another, the researcher knew it was the reseller, not the model provider, that was responsible.
Last, the canary experiment revealed that some providers are scraping secret URLs put into the prompts, in violation of privacy terms. Moore wrote:

The clearest example involves a Chinese AI lab. This lab’s systems fetched the secret URLs from more than half of the prompts that we sent to its models between July and October, including roughly two-thirds of the requests marked as “no data collection” or Zero Data Retention. The scraper typically showed up two or three days after the request. This wasn’t limited to requests sent to the lab directly. Several US hosting providers resell this lab’s models, and prompts sent to those providers triggered the exact same scraper—the prompts were flowing back to the lab. A customer who picked a US provider specifically to keep their data in the U.S. didn’t get what they paid for. Later on, a git client on a different cloud started trying to clone the private repositories referenced in our prompts, but only for prompts that used this lab’s models.

This wasn’t limited to requests sent to the lab directly. Several US hosting providers resell this lab’s models, and prompts sent to those providers triggered the exact same scraper—the prompts were flowing back to the lab. A customer who picked a US provider specifically to keep their data in the U.S. didn’t get what they paid for. Later on, a git client on a different cloud started trying to clone the private repositories referenced in our prompts, but only for prompts that used this lab’s models.

The researcher said he found one US hosting provider crawling a secret URL more than two months after it was used in a single inference call to its search endpoint. Another ran a scraper that came back for URLs days after each request, regardless of the AI router used to reach it.

Moore said that the most effective means for preventing leakage is to host models using on-premises servers. That option is expensive, though. For those who can’t afford a self-hosted system, the next best option, Moore said, is to receive service directly from a first-tier provider that provides “one contract and a privacy policy to read.” Moore said that even then, there’s no guarantee no data will leak, but that the measure minimizes the chances. AI users should also avoid accepting default provider or reseller pools and instead pick upstream providers themselves.

The blockbuster research is the latest indictment exposing the lax privacy and security that’s endemic in much of the AI ecosystem. The findings mean that people who want to ensure secrets they put into prompts stay private face a daunting task that isn’t likely to become easier any time soon.

news.title: OpenAI makes it much harder for attackers to extract how its latest AI models think
news.title_en: OpenAI makes it much harder for attackers to extract how its latest AI models think
news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.article_content:
OpenAI has sharply tightened safeguards against extracting internal reasoning from GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. In internal automated tests, attacks pulling protected reasoning from prior requests dropped from a 54.0 percent success rate on GPT-6 Astra to 0.2 percent on GPT-6.2 Astra. Attacks on active requests fell from 22.9 to 0.9 percent, OpenAI says. The company is now bringing selected improvements to GPT-6 Astra, too.

The defenses work on two levels. For individual requests, the systems combine targeted training, input and output filters for messages and tool calls, and API blocks that stop older models from reading protected reasoning. Against coordinated campaigns, OpenAI bans thousands to tens of thousands of accounts weekly.

Attack success rate (ASR) in adaptive black-box red teaming against GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.2 Astra, aggregated across six attacker models. Lower is better.

Anthropic is fighting systematic distillation attacks as well, also banning tens of thousands of accounts to curb the theft of internal reasoning, reportedly succeeding in 90 to 99 percent of cases. Anthropic has also called for a coordinated response from industry and policymakers.

news.title_zh: OpenAI强化推理层防护，抑制大模型蒸馏攻击
news.summary_zh: OpenAI大幅提升GPT-6.2系列模型安全性，通过多层过滤机制将推理数据泄露攻击成功率降至0.2%以下

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI针对GPT-6.2 Astra与GPT-6.2 Sol模型部署了分层防护机制，通过针对性训练、输入输出过滤及API拦截策略，将针对推理数据的黑盒攻击成功率从54%大幅削减至0.2%。该举措旨在阻断通过合成数据蒸馏提取模型核心推理模式的攻击链路，并配合每周对数万违规账户的封禁实现全链条防御。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI has deployed layered security mechanisms for GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models, reducing the success rate of black-box inference-extraction attacks from 54% to under 0.2% through targeted training, input/output filtering, and API access restrictions. These measures are designed to neutralize distillation attacks that attempt to reconstruct core reasoning paths, supplemented by the weekly suspension of tens of thousands of illicit accounts.

elements_zh.who: OpenAI（模型开发者）
elements_zh.where: 企业内部模型安全生产环境
elements_zh.what: 部署针对推理数据的多层防护架构，包括输入/输出过滤、API访问拦截及针对性强化训练
elements_zh.why: 防止攻击者通过模型蒸馏技术窃取核心推理逻辑，保护模型技术壁垒

elements_en.what: Implemented layered defenses including I/O filtering, API blocking, and adversarial training
elements_en.why: To prevent distillation-based theft of internal reasoning logic and protect proprietary model intellectual property

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 大模型竞争已进入以‘知识产权保全’为核心的防蒸馏防御战阶段。随着模型推理逻辑的价值攀升，闭源大模型厂商正通过强化API黑盒化与流量合规清洗，从底层逻辑上切断廉价获取高质量蒸馏数据的路径，这将迫使后续开源模型生态面临更严苛的训练数据合规审查压力。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Competition in the large model sector has shifted toward intellectual property preservation via anti-distillation defense. As reasoning logic becomes a primary value driver, proprietary model vendors are increasingly 'black-boxing' APIs and cleansing traffic to block cost-effective distillation, likely forcing the open-source community to face significantly higher scrutiny regarding training data provenance.

news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone and Telefónica are in early talks to form a consortium that would bid for European satellite spectrum and offer calls, texts and data to ordinary phones from orbit, Bloomberg reported on Monday. The service would compete with Starlink on its home continent.

Paula Doenecke, Gian Volpicelli and Clara Hernanz Lizarraga cited people familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified. No decision has been taken on the consortium or on whether it will bid, they said. All four operators declined to comment to Bloomberg. TNW has not independently verified the report.

The prize is a slice of the 2 GHz band that Brussels wants to reserve for a European-controlled operator. The four companies together serve most of the mobile customers in the EU’s largest markets. If they bid as one, the reserved third of the band has an obvious winner before the auction opens.

The band in question is the 2 GHz mobile satellite services spectrum, a 30 MHz pairing that lets a handset keep a connection where no mast reaches. The current licences, held by Viasat and EchoStar since 2009, expire in May 2027. The European Commission proposed on 27 May to run a single EU-level selection for the next licences and to split the band in three.

One third would go to a company under majority European control. One third would go to sovereign government services, delivered through IRIS², the EU’s own constellation. The final third would be open to anyone, including SpaceX and Amazon. TNW reported the shape of the plan the day before the Commission adopted it.

The proposal still has to pass the European Parliament and the Council. The carriers are organising for an auction whose rules do not yet exist in law.

Direct-to-device is the one satellite service that reaches a mass market without new hardware, and Starlink dominates it. SpaceX can already send texts, data and calls to unmodified phones from orbit, and it sells that capability through mobile operators, including Deutsche Telekom, Bloomberg noted. What it cannot do in the EU is offer the service on its own, because it does not hold the spectrum.

That is the leverage the consortium would be bidding for. An operator that holds the European third of the band decides whether Starlink is a supplier or a competitor in its market. Four operators holding it together decide that for most of the continent.

The awkward part is that two of the four already have American partners. Deutsche Telekom has an agreement with SpaceX to offer Starlink’s direct-to-device service. Vodafone owns half of a joint venture with AST SpaceMobile, the Texas company building its own phone-to-satellite network. Vodafone owns half of a joint venture with AST SpaceMobile, the Texas company building its own phone-to-satellite network. Under the Commission’s proposal, that 50/50 structure would not qualify as European-controlled, and Vodafone would have to change it to bid, Bloomberg reported.
So the consortium is not four carriers versus America. It is four carriers deciding how much of America they want inside the tent.

Brussels has spent 2026 tilting the space market towards European firms. IRIS² went from plan to full deployment in August, with 348 satellites and a bill above €15bn. The EU Space Act would put any operator serving EU users under prior authorisation. Washington has lobbied against it, and four American space companies pulled out of Macron’s Paris summit this week under White House pressure.
The spectrum reservation is the sharpest of those tools, because spectrum is finite and a licence lasts years. Reserve a third for Europe and Starlink is capped at a third, whatever it builds.

The gap is the satellites. Reserving spectrum for a European operator does not create a European constellation. IRIS² will not enter service until 2029, will start with broadband rather than phones, and its direct-to-mobile capability is limited and comes through Hispasat, Bloomberg reported. A four-carrier consortium would win the right to use the band before it has anything to use it with.

Europe’s own direct-to-device candidates are small. Spain’s Sateliot is seeking €150m to beam 5G to phones. Eutelsat, the largest European operator, is still waiting for growth to return in 2027. Amazon, meanwhile, has asked the FCC for 5,105 satellites dedicated to phones. The likeliest outcome is that a European consortium holds the spectrum and leases capacity from an American constellation until a European one exists.

The four companies in the talks are the incumbents of Germany, France, Britain and Spain. A joint venture between them, holding an exclusive national-security-flavoured spectrum block, would be one of the largest telecoms combinations Europe has seen. Brussels has spent two decades blocking or conditioning far smaller carrier tie-ups.

The same Commission that wrote the sovereignty rule would have to clear the joint venture that exploits it. That is not a contradiction, but it is a choice, and the competition directorate has not yet had to make it.

Three things. The first is the legislation. Parliament and Council have to pass the 2 GHz regulation before May 2027, or the current licences lapse into a vacuum. The carriers are organising around a deadline the legislators have not yet committed to.
The second is Vodafone. If it restructures the AST joint venture to qualify, the consortium is real. If it does not, the consortium is three carriers and a problem.

The third is who supplies the satellites. A European-controlled licensee flying on Starlink or AST capacity satisfies the letter of the rule. Whether it satisfies the reason for the rule is the argument Europe will be having in 2027.

news.article_content:
NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip giant.

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at the company.

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.

The crisis has sent shares in Nvidia, a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing.

paragraphs: NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip giant.

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at the company.
A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.

Still, the accounting focus of the probe, which Reuters is reporting for the first time, increases pressure on Nvidia, whose investors are still reeling from revelations about ousted CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital relationships, including with Alice Huang, who US authorities suspect is a Chinese spy. China has denied she is a spy.

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week.
The crisis has sent shares in Nvidia, a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing.

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted "lawful business." Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The SEC probe is the latest of Nvidia's legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported last month.
SINGAPORE ACCOUNTING CHANGE BACK IN FOCUS

Last year, Nvidia changed how it reports geographic revenue, using customer headquarters rather than billing addresses, which it said would better reflect the geographic profile of its revenue. The change resulted in Singapore being removed from its geographical breakdown.
The Financial Times, citing company accounts, reported on Tuesday that Nvidia had made the change even as Singapore sales soared to almost half its global revenue.
That accounting shift has drawn renewed press scrutiny in the wake of the Alice Huang scandal.
Southeast Asia has become a hub for chip smuggling to China since the Biden administration barred advanced AI chip exports to that country over concerns they could boost Beijing’s military.

Analysts and investors have also grown increasingly concerned about circular AI financing deals, in which chipmakers including Nvidia have pursued complex financial arrangements to help customers fund purchases of their chips and the construction of costly AI infrastructure, such as data centers. Nvidia has backed AI companies and cloud providers and provided guarantees connected to data-center projects that use its equipment.

Critics say such arrangements can make it harder for investors to assess the quality of chipmakers' revenue and their true financial exposure. Speaking to Reuters last month, SEC enforcement chief David Woodcock said the agency was examining AI companies' corporate disclosures to ensure issuers are giving investors the full picture on potential risks.

On its Tuesday earnings call, Nvidia's interim CEO and former CFO Colette Kress said the company was proud of its role in supporting the AI industry, but would be far more selective moving forward about AI industry financing deals.

The SEC under President Donald Trump has pulled back on enforcement, saying it will focus on bread-and-butter securities fraud, including accounting violations that have long been a mainstay of its enforcement work. It recently launched a new financial reporting and accounting unit within its enforcement division, aimed at developing cases in accounting and auditing areas.

news.title: Nvidia stock plunges 12%, rides longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis
news.title_en: Nvidia stock plunges 12%, rides longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis
news.author: Kif Leswing
news.article_content:
The last time Wall Street was this down on Nvidia the chipmaker's flagship product was the GeForce graphics processor for high-end PC video games, and markets were reeling from the global financial crisis.

Nvidia shares fell 12% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang. The stock is poised to close lower for a seventh consecutive week, the longest such stretch since 2008.

Shares of Nvidia are down 44% over the period, pushing the company's market cap down by $2.5 trillion. The stock is now trading at around 9.3 times forward earnings, while Advanced Micro Devices is valued at 29 times profit for the next 12 months.

On Friday, Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is exploring potential accounting issues at Nvidia, pushing the stock down further.

Once the most valuable company, now, at a market cap of $3.1 trillion, Nvidia is fourth behind Apple and Microsoft and Alphabet.

Nvidia is reeling from the removal of Huang, who resigned on Nov. 12, after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly a spy.

Harvey Jones, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, said earlier this week that Huang had resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms."

But the chipmaker's losing streak started before Nvidia was thrown into crisis as investors worried over the sustainability of the AI buildout, particularly after the midterm elections, and emerging competition in AI chips from Google and AMD.

Even a better-than-expected earnings report, which included an increase to fiscal 2028 guidance, didn't stem the selling. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the company's longtime CFO, projected revenue growth next fiscal year of 75%, and said that customers aren't going anywhere.

On Tuesday's earnings call with analysts, Kress signed off by saying, "we've got this."In a company meeting the next day, executives told staff that it was moving its yearly review process, which can come with more stock, from March to December.

For investors, one major question is whether Nvidia can continue to innovate and sustain its commanding lead in the AI chip market without its visionary leader. Almost the entire company now is built around the AI trade, a phenomenon that began taking hold just four years ago with the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT.

Before that, Nvidia's primary business was selling graphics cards used for video games. In mid-2008, the last time the stock was this deep into a weekly losing streak, Nvidia was generating less than $1 billion per quarter. Now it pulls in more than $1 billion per day. Almost the entire company now is built around the AI trade, a phenomenon that began taking hold just four years ago with the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT.

Before that, Nvidia's primary business was selling graphics cards used for video games. In mid-2008, the last time the stock was this deep into a weekly losing streak, Nvidia was generating less than $1 billion per quarter. Now it pulls in more than $1 billion per day. At the time, the entire market was in freefall due to the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

Should a deal materialize, it would represent the inaugural major deployment for Helix, which launched in June under former Amazon Web Services chief executive Adam Selipsky after raising roughly $11 billion from KKR's balance sheet alongside backers including Nvidia Corp. and the Kuwait Investment Authority.

For KKR, acquiring EdgeCore would bolster a sprawling data center portfolio that already includes CyrusOne and reinforce its commitment to AI infrastructure following its participation in a $500 billion chip-financing pact with Nvidia and Wall Street peers earlier this year. Meanwhile, a sale would offer a lucrative exit for Partners Group, which acquired EdgeCore in 2022 with an initial $1.2 billion capital commitment before injecting an additional $1.9 billion to scale its operations.

The talks unfold against a shifting backdrop for data center operators and their financial sponsors. Industry sentiment has recently been tested by heightened regulatory scrutiny following Democratic gains in the midterm elections, increased caution from banks managing a glut of AI-related debt, and leadership upheaval at strategic partner Nvidia following this month's ouster of CEO Jensen Huang.

Ultimately, a completed transaction would establish a closely watched valuation benchmark for buyout firms seeking liquidity from early AI infrastructure bets. Many institutional investors have struggled to price data center assets still awaiting power grid connections and regulatory permits, leaving private equity sponsors searching for viable exit pathways as the sector matures.

news.title: Take-Two says GTA VI generated $3.79B in day-one sales, surpassing the $2.9B lifetime box-office gross of the highest-grossing film Avengers: Endgame (Jennifer Maas/Variety)
news.title_en: Take-Two says GTA VI generated $3.79B in day-one sales, surpassing the $2.9B lifetime box-office gross of the highest-grossing film Avengers: Endgame (Jennifer Maas/Variety)
news.author: Variety
news.article_content:
Crime pays: Rockstar Games’ “Grand Theft Auto 6″ preorder and first-day sales reached $3.79 billion, the game developer announced Friday.

Per Rockstar Games parent company Take-Two Interactive, that total sets “a new record for entertainment across any medium” and makes “GTA 6” “the biggest entertainment launch in history.”

For the sake of comparison, Sony Pictures’ “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” reaped $2.52 billion at the global box office in 2026, the No. 1 movie of the year to date. Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster “The Odyssey” has taken in just over $1.8 billion to date.

On its first day of release, “GTA 6” made roughly as much as James Cameron’s last two “Avatar” movies, “The Way of Water” and “Fire and Ash,” have grossed combined. With just Day 1 sales, “GTA 6” has already out-grossed the highest grossing movie of all time, “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.9 billion), in one day.

“GTA 6” launched Thursday for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S and was also available on Xbox One via Xbox’s Cloud Gaming service. The game retails at $80 for the standard edition and $100 for the ultimate version. Preorders for “GTA 6” opened June 25.

With a reported total gameplay time of approximately 80 hours to complete its main storyline, “GTA 6” follows duo Jason and Lucia as they navigate their way through criminal life in the fictional Leonida.

“GTA 6” has reached a 99 Metacritic score (tying it for the highest-rated video game of all time) and received a nomination for Game of the Year at The Game Awards this December.

“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI,’” Rockstar Games president and founder Sam Houser said. “We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”

news.title: Jensen Huang’s ‘Lying’ Alarmed Nvidia Board Ahead of His Resignation
news.title_en: Jensen Huang’s ‘Lying’ Alarmed Nvidia Board Ahead of His Resignation
news.author: Lauren Goode and Paresh Dave
news.article_content:
Jensen Huang was ousted from Nvidia amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Yet it was “multiple issues” related to Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying” that ultimately moved the board of directors, according to two people familiar with private discussions among the chair and other members.

While Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang on November 8, the board couldn’t determine in the moment whether she was an intelligence operative for China, these sources say. That same day, the board announced an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting” that their CEO had “been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has rejected allegations that Alice Huang was a spy.

But in the following days, once allegations of other affairs surfaced, including one reportedly with a direct report, “what could be determined was [Huang’s] lying, and that spanned a year, from October 2025 through recent events,” a source close to the board told WIRED, who requested anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak on its behalf.

According to sources, members of the board had asked Huang about Alice Huang after The New York Times first reported in October 2025 that Nvidia had an unusually robust business relationship with a Singapore-based data center company named Megaspeed, where Alice Huang worked. Jensen Huang at the time denied any inappropriate relationship with Alice Huang to the board, sources tell WIRED.

After the affair came to light, the board was incensed, these people say. A source familiar with the board’s thinking told WIRED that while these board members view issues of national security as “important” and “ongoing,” the primary driver behind Huang’s ouster was “the lying.”

“It was a matter of integrity and trust,” this person said.

In recent days, board members, including chair Harvey Jones, have tried to quell the discourse about Huang’s possible return to Nvidia by emphasizing that Huang's behavior flew in the face of Nvidia’s policies and corporate governance rules, sources tell WIRED. While previous reporting by WIRED and other news outlets have outlined factors that Jones has said played into the board’s decision, the primary motivation hadn’t been previously specified.

Board chair Harvey Jones did not respond to a WIRED request for comment. A spokesperson for Nvidia, John Rizzo, declined to comment. John Fisher, vice president at the communications firm Trident, which is representing Huang, declined to comment except to say that Huang voluntarily resigned from his positions at Nvidia.

news.summary_en: Nvidia's board of directors ousted CEO Jensen Huang after an investigation confirmed he misled the board for a year regarding his relationship with an employee at Singapore-based Megaspeed and potential national security implications. While external reports focused on foreign intelligence ties, Board Chair Harvey Jones cited a fundamental lack of integrity and violation of corporate governance policies as the primary drivers for the termination.
paragraphs: Jensen Huang was ousted from Nvidia amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Yet it was “multiple issues” related to Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying” that ultimately moved the board of directors, according to two people familiar with private discussions among the chair and other members.

While Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang on November 8, the board couldn’t determine in the moment whether she was an intelligence operative for China, these sources say. That same day, the board announced an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting” that their CEO had “been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has rejected allegations that Alice Huang was a spy.

But in the following days, once allegations of other affairs surfaced, including one reportedly with a direct report, “what could be determined was [Huang’s] lying, and that spanned a year, from October 2025 through recent events,” a source close to the board told WIRED, who requested anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak on its behalf.

According to sources, members of the board had asked Huang about Alice Huang after The New York Times first reported in October 2025 that Nvidia had an unusually robust business relationship with a Singapore-based data center company named Megaspeed, where Alice Huang worked. Jensen Huang at the time denied any inappropriate relationship with Alice Huang to the board, sources tell WIRED.

After the affair came to light, the board was incensed, these people say. A source familiar with the board’s thinking told WIRED that while these board members view issues of national security as “important” and “ongoing,” the primary driver behind Huang’s ouster was “the lying.”
“It was a matter of integrity and trust,” this person said.

In recent days, board members, including chair Harvey Jones, have tried to quell the discourse about Huang’s possible return to Nvidia by emphasizing that Huang's behavior flew in the face of Nvidia’s policies and corporate governance rules, sources tell WIRED. While previous reporting by WIRED and other news outlets have outlined factors that Jones has said played into the board’s decision, the primary motivation hadn’t been previously specified.

Board chair Harvey Jones did not respond to a WIRED request for comment. A spokesperson for Nvidia, John Rizzo, declined to comment. John Fisher, vice president at the communications firm Trident, which is representing Huang, declined to comment except to say that Huang voluntarily resigned from his positions at Nvidia.

For Nvidia’s board, the possibility that Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government poses a bigger problem than an executive’s personal misconduct. If she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, the scandal isn’t just about Huang’s alleged “lack of candor,” but a potential security and governance crisis.

Already the scandal has given China hawks grist to call for tighter controls on US business dealings with China. In addition, multiple government agencies and offices have called for investigations into what the former Nvidia CEO may have known about the company’s chips getting into China. The company’s general counsel Tim Teter has also been called to Washington, DC to testify, as government officials try to find out more about Nvidia’s possible flouting of export controls.

Nvidia and Huang are also facing several shareholder lawsuits, alleging the CEO and the company made misleading statements about dealings with Alice Huang and Megaspeed. Other Silicon Valley investors have publicly raised concerns about insufficient corporate governance and executive oversight by the board.

In the company’s all-hands meeting on November 18, board chair Jones said it was “not an easy decision to accept [Huang’s] resignation,” according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. “However, the disclosure of personal behavior and a lack of candor inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and values made this a necessary decision.”

Meanwhile, fans and supporters of Huang, including thousands of Nvidia employees and Elon Musk, have continued to call for his return to Nvidia. Huang himself has said he would be “honored” to come back as CEO. On Friday, US President Donald Trump renewed his call for Huang to have another chance. “He made some bad decisions, but he is a brilliant person,” Trump told reporters. “I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology.”

The news outlet Semafor reported that a small faction of Nvidia’s board of directors has pushed to bring Huang back as well. Jones has not responded to WIRED’s inquiries about the board’s reported division on the topic of Huang’s return.

Some employees are miffed at how quickly the board accepted Huang’s resignation, insisting the longtime leader must have been the victim of a coordinated campaign intended to unseat him. “We feel like they forced his hands to resign,” says one person on the business side at Nvidia. “We don’t understand why the board is so adamant about not giving him a second chance.”

At the all-hands meeting, interim CEO Colette Kress said employees’ biggest concern was Nvidia’s falling share price. The next biggest concern was the board’s decision to oust Huang. But while she addressed the first by moving up pay raises, she offered no promise on sharing results of the board’s investigation into Huang or its deliberations about him.
“The ship has sinked but there’s no plan to be transparent about what happened,” says one computer scientist working at Nvidia. “It feels like a black box.”

news.title: Signal blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and Android to stop AI agents from reading private chats
news.title_en: Signal blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and Android to stop AI agents from reading private chats
news.author: Manuel Uth
news.article_content:
Signal is restricting screenshots to stop AI agents from reading private chats. The app blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and triggers protection on supported Android versions when an AI assistant tries to access the screen. Signal warned Reuters of an "existential threat"to privacy.

OS-level AI like Apple's Siri AI and Google's Gemini Intelligence can capture screen content to complete user tasks. That undermines end-to-end encryption by letting agents pull decrypted messages straight from the display and process them externally.

Meta's AI agent Muse recently captured Signal content on Android and macOS through broad setup permissions, including accessibility tools and screenshots on macOS. Meta says this happened only with explicit user permission.

Signal already blocked Microsoft's Recall on Windows but calls its defenses incomplete: macOS screenshots can't be reliably blocked, and AI access to file systems and notifications remains a risk. Signal says Apple, Google, and Microsoft should make it easy to block AI agents from apps entirely.

news.title: Canada Retail Sales Tracking Largest Decline Since Feb. 2025
news.title_en: Canada Retail Sales Tracking Largest Decline Since Feb. 2025
news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
Canadian retail spending is expected to have declined in October, following a 0.8% increase in September led by gasoline stations and fuel vendors.

A preliminary estimate points to a 1.5% decrease in retail sales last month, which would be the largest decline since February 2025.

Sales in September increased in five out of nine subsectors, and rose by 6.9% at gasoline stations and fuel vendors. That increase was largely driven by higher prices, as sales in volume terms increased by a more modest 1.6%.

Economists surveyed by Bloomberg had expected retail sales increased by 0.7% in September.

Core retail sales, which exclude gasoline stations and fuel vendors as well as motor vehicle and parts dealers, increased by 0.1%. In volume terms, sales were also up by 0.1%.

The largest decline in core retail sales was food and beverage retailers, which was led by a 0.5% decline at grocery stores, following a 1% increase in August.

Building material and garden equipment and supplies dealers declined by 1.3%, while furniture, home furnishings electronics and appliances retailers decreased by the same magnitude.

Meanwhile, retail sales increased by 1.2% in the third quarter. In volume terms, they rose by 1% over the three-month period.

The expected decline in October retail sales provides further evidence of weakening to start the fourth quarter, said CIBC senior economist Andrew Grantham.

“While the 1.5% decline estimated for October will partly reflect lower gasoline prices, most of that move lower in pump prices has actually occurred in November rather than October, and as a result this advance estimate suggests a decline in volumes as well,” Grantham said in a note to investors.

The Canadian economy — including consumer spending — has remained largely resilient throughout the U.S. trade war. However, growth is expected to slow in the second half of the year after the dispute escalated and more tariffs were imposed by both countries.

The labour market has also shown signs of weakness, as employment has failed to grow this year. Servus Credit Union chief economist Charles St-Arnaud said the stagnant labour market in recent months may be to blame for weaker retail sales.

“This is another indicator that suggests that the Canadian economy is losing momentum going into the last few months of 2026. The weakness suggests the Bank of Canada should take a pause to better assess the situation before hike again, especially with some fuel prices easing in recent weeks,” St-Arnaud said in an email.

Despite the expected slowdown, the Bank of Canada raised interest rates in October to clamp down on inflationary pressures from higher energy prices. Traders in overnight swaps put the odds of a hike in December at about 60%, which would further weigh on spending.

news.title: Google's Gemini can now run Mac apps and finish desktop chores in the background while you keep working
news.title_en: Google's Gemini can now run Mac apps and finish desktop chores in the background while you keep working
news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.article_content:
Google now lets Gemini handle Mac tasks in the background. The new "Computer Use"feature in the Gemini Mac app completes multistep tasks across local files, desktop apps, and websites. Google says users simply describe a goal, and Gemini clicks, types, and navigates menus and forms. Everything runs in an isolated background window with a live chat preview, keeping the screen and cursor free for uninterrupted work.

Users choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause anytime, and approve key actions beforehand. Google's examples include batch-editing photos and 3D scenes, filling out shipping forms from local PDFs, and building presentations.

Computer Use rolls out in English in the US today, and the Gemini Mac app is available to download. OpenAI has also focused on Computer Use recently, pulling well ahead with its Astra model.

news.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US
news.title_en: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US
news.author: Lauren Feiner
news.article_content:
President Donald Trump promised to put a “tremendous tax” on companies that build data centers outside of the US, even as states and cities around the country are placing restrictions on new applications to build them.

“We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country,” Trump said at a press conference Friday following his summit with China President Xi Jinping and Russia President Vladimir Putin. “They allowed that to happen with chips and everything else, and it was very destructive to our country. It’s where we started going behind.” Should the US allow data centers to be built outside of the country, Trump warned, “China will take them all.”

Trump didn’t share many details behind the plan, and apparently was floating the proposal publicly for the first time. “I don’t know if that’s a breaking story. But I haven’t even said that to my people,” Trump said, flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. “But I’m telling them now. They’re here. Many of them are here.”

Trump’s promise could be difficult to fulfill with a new Democratic majority Congress being sworn in within a couple of months. Even members of his own party recognize that the data center buildout has become an unpopular issue across the board. With states installing moratoriums and new restrictions on data center proposals, companies may be forced to look outside of the country, but Trump’s threat is an attempt to make that a less attractive alternative.
